images.caption: Figure 1:TwinLab-Bench covers 52 tasks by division and department, and a separate TwinLab agent drives the environment of each task.

Figure 2:Two axes for science benchmarks.(a) From left to right, the agent designs more of the method, and TwinLab-Bench tests ability ④. (b) From left to right, the environment for new experiments comes closer to a real laboratory, and TwinLab-Bench uses environment ③.
Figure 4:How a task is run.The task materials of one example task, and one run with the actor, TwinLab, and judge agents.

Figure 5:Scorecard of science benchmarks.Each row is a benchmark, and each bar splits its tasks by the levels in the key of its column. Orange boxes mark the main weakness of each group of benchmarks.
Figure 6:Mean score versus the cost of the actor agent; models run at high effort by default.
Table 3:Actor agents’ conclusions when the true state changes.We keep the handoff word for word and change only the true state of the laboratory.
Table 4:Closed-book memory probesof Opus 5.5 on all tasks. Bars give the number of tasks with a yes, partial, or no answer.

Table 7:Main results.Mean score (0 to 100) of each actor agent and reasoning effort by academic division, by task form, and over all tasks (All), together with the cost of the actor agent on all tasks in USD. GPT-6.1-sol at low effort has no valid run on one task.
